_notes.throttling: The throttling block is Lighthouse's 'Slow 4G' profile (constants.throttling.mobileSlow4G): 150ms RTT and 1.6Mbps with the CPU slowed 4x, which is what §2's 'on 4G networks' target means. Under the devtools method Chrome itself is throttled with requestLatencyMs 562.5 (150 x 3.75), downloadThroughputKbps 1474.56 (1638.4 x 0.9), uploadThroughputKbps 675 (750 x 0.9) and cpuSlowdownMultiplier 4. rttMs and throughputKbps are read only by the simulate method and stay so the block remains the profile Lighthouse names. The desktop preset brings its own desktopDense4G (40ms RTT, 10Mbps, no CPU slowdown, no applied latency); these values override it key by key, and every report's configSettings.throttling shows the six values above.
_notes.throttlingMethod: devtools, not simulate. Simulate loads the page unthrottled and Lantern replays the request graph at the profile's speed. On localhost a Next App Router page's framework chunks finish before first paint, so Lantern counts them as render-blocking and charges their whole download at 1.6Mbps to LCP, although the observed LCP equals FCP. Measured under simulate with these settings: the real /sv/login markup with every script removed and the same CSS scored LCP 751-902ms, and a Next route with no client components and no messages, only the framework runtime, scored LCP 2031-2049ms. No App Router page could reach 1200ms however little it shipped, so the gate measured the model rather than the page. devtools applies the same latency, throughput and CPU slowdown to the real load and reports what Chrome observed. The budgets (LCP 1200ms, TTI 1500ms, TBT 100ms, CLS 0.1, accessibility 100) and every other assertion are unchanged. On 2026-09-13, on a shared machine under load, the three URLs gave LCP 1470-1515ms, TTI 2060-2101ms, TBT 27-43ms, CLS 0 and accessibility 100 over nine runs, so the gate is still red on LCP and TTI. In those reports the document arrives after ~600ms and the render-blocking stylesheet after ~1400ms, one applied 562.5ms request latency each, before anything can paint. Measured the same way, the real markup with every script removed and the same stylesheet scored LCP 1273-1369ms: under this profile no page that waits for an external stylesheet paints within 1200ms, however little JavaScript it ships. A Next route with only the framework runtime (five scripts, 150KB) scored LCP 1519-1611ms and TTI 2099-2142ms, its last script arriving after ~1990ms; the pages sit on that floor, so TTI 1500ms is not reachable while they wait for the runtime either.
_notes.inp: INP is a field metric — it needs real user interactions and cannot be measured in a lab run. total-blocking-time is asserted at the same 100ms threshold as the closest lab proxy, and max-potential-fid is a warning only because it is noisy. Enforcing the real INP ≤ 100ms target requires RUM (web-vitals reporting to an analytics endpoint); this file cannot substitute for that.
_notes.interactive: 'interactive' is Lighthouse's Time to Interactive audit. It is deprecated upstream and may be removed in a future major; if it disappears, replace with total-blocking-time plus speed-index rather than dropping the TTI gate silently.
_notes.accessibility: categories:accessibility minScore 1 is the 'Lighthouse accessibility score = 100' requirement. Like axe-core it covers only automatable checks; AA conformance still needs a manual keyboard and screen-reader pass.
